clue.text: Post selection of Christmas tidings

indicators.note: selection of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Seasonal greetings arriving in the post, a handful picked from the pile.
explanation.definitionFit: A post is an upright pole, the same thing as a ship's mast in a general sense.

clue.text: Island briefly manufactured a vehicle without petrol

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word for manufactured loses its last letter

parts.note: made means manufactured

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so a vehicle goes round the petrol

parts.note: taken as written
a car is a vehicle
gas is the American word for petrol

explanation.surface: On an island, a car was built that needs no fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; petrol is called gas in American English.
explanation.definitionFit: Madagascar is a large island nation off the south-east coast of Africa.

clue.text: Champion winning in tennis, perhaps

indicators.note: in says the word for winning sits inside the word for tennis

parts.note: tennis is an example of a sport
up means ahead or winning, as in two sets up

explanation.surface: A title-holder on the way to victory at tennis, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champion' is a verb here: to champion a cause is to back it.
explanation.definitionFit: To champion something is to back or advocate it, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Member of wedding party travels, with mother in command

indicators.note: in says the travelling and the mother sit inside the word for a command

parts.note: to bid is to command
rides means travels, on horseback or in a vehicle
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Someone at a wedding is getting about, with mum firmly in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridesmaid attends the bride, so she belongs to the wedding party.

clue.text: One singer at far end of Tower Bridge

indicators.note: at the far end of means the last letter of tower

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
an alto is a singer of the low female or high male voice part

explanation.surface: A lone vocalist stands at the far end of Tower Bridge in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tower Bridge' reads as the London landmark, but the two words split: Tower gives a letter and Bridge is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto is the famous old bridge over the Grand Canal in Venice.

clue.text: Confuse old man swallowing one medium-sized tranquilliser

indicators.note: swallowing means taking in, so the word for confuse goes round one

parts.note: to daze is to stun or confuse
I is the Roman numeral for one
pa is an informal word for father, one's old man
M is the clothing size medium

explanation.surface: A bewildered father gulps down a moderate dose of sedative.
explanation.definitionFit: Diazepam, sold as Valium, is a widely used sedative drug.

clue.text: Note used in Peruvian currency

definitions.meaning: in tonic ...-fa, the fifth note of the scale

explanation.definitionFit: Sol is both the sol-fa syllable for the fifth note and the name of Peru's currency.

clue.text: A repeated note lute played in small band

indicators.note: repeated means the note letter appears twice

parts.note: N, a common crossword abbreviation for note

indicators.note: played means the letters of lute are performed in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: One note over and over on a lute by a little group of musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small band' sounds like a combo of players, but it means a thin ring.
explanation.definitionFit: An annulet is a small ring or fillet, as on a column in architecture.

clue.text: Colour expert is terrible, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word for terrible is heard, not spelt

parts.note: dire means terrible

explanation.surface: A colour consultant is awful, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: A dyer colours cloth for a living, so knows a lot about colour.

clue.text: Discussion about where indecisive people are found round about

parts.note: c, circa, means about

indicators.note: round means placed around, so the earlier pieces encircle the second about

parts.note: undecided people are said to sit on the fence
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A talk about where undecided folk sit, roughly speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: C plus ON FENCE gives CONFENCE, which 'round' wraps about RE, after CONFE.
explanation.definitionFit: A conference is a formal meeting for discussion.

clue.text: After brief decline, see graduate getting qualification

indicators.note: after places seeing and the graduate behind the short decline

parts.note: a dip is a brief drop or decline
lo is an old word meaning see! or look!
MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: Following a short slump, a student finally earns their certificate.
explanation.definitionFit: A diploma is a certificate awarded for completing a course of study.

clue.text: Former president completely ruined? Not completely

parts.note: all means completely, as in all gone

indicators.note: not completely says the word for ruined loses its last letter

parts.note: ended, in the sense of finished off or destroyed

explanation.surface: Was an ex-leader's regime a total wreck? Only partly.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador Allende was President of Chile from 1970 until the coup of 1973.

clue.text: Be mad to take sudden dislike to waders?

parts.note: to go off something is to suddenly stop liking it
rails are wading marsh birds; with the article, the wading birds

explanation.surface: Is it madness to suddenly hate one's fishing boots?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waders' looks like rubber boots, but it means birds: rails are long-legged birds of marshes.
explanation.definitionFit: To go off the rails is an idiom for losing one's mind or behaving wildly.

clue.text: See 12
Shortly feel embarrassed during play about Lancashire town

indicators.note: during says the embarrassment comes within the word for play

parts.note: to act is to play a part

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to cringe is to feel embarrassed
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A playgoer briefly winces during a drama about a northern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancashire is a county in north-west England; 'Shortly' clips the last letter before 'during' places the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Accrington is a mill town in Lancashire, famous for its football club Accrington Stanley.

clue.text: Protect lad, waving implement — that's shocking!

indicators.note: waving means moving about, so the letters of protect lad are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone tells a boy to shield himself from a gadget being brandished: it delivers a jolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A cattle prod is a stick that gives livestock a mild electric shock to move them.

clue.text: Educated woman's bowled over by European lampoon

indicators.note: bowled over means knocked flat, so the woman's name is turned backwards

parts.note: Rita is the woman in the play and film Educating Rita, so Rita's

explanation.surface: A learned lady is overwhelmed by a European's mocking piece.
explanation.walkthrough: Educating Rita is Willy Russell's play about a hairdresser who goes to university.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire is a lampoon: writing that ridicules its target through mockery.

clue.text: US state axed army in old port

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California
cut means axed, as a job or programme is
TA is the Territorial Army, the British volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: An American state disbanded its forces in a historic harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Calcutta, now Kolkata, is the former name of the great Indian seaport on the Hooghly.

clue.text: A bit shattered, Henry covers only half of London sporting event

indicators.note: in a down clue, covers puts the letter on top of what follows
shattered means broken up, so the letters of a bit are rearranged

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

indicators.note: only half of means just the first three letters of London

explanation.surface: A worn-out Henry reports on only part of a sporting event in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A biathlon is a winter sports race combining cross-country skiing and rifle shooting.

clue.text: A writer fills page ten in French section of book

indicators.note: fills says the writer goes inside the page and the French ten

parts.note: dix is French for ten
a pen is something you write with

explanation.surface: Someone writes on a tenth page in French as part of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: An appendix is supplementary material at the end of a book.

clue.text: Key player is overshadowed by very good worker

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means very good

indicators.note: overshadowed by means covered by, so is sits within the following pieces

parts.note: an ant is the classic worker insect
taken as written

explanation.surface: A star team member is outshone by an excellent colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key player' looks like a vital team member, but keys are piano keys.
explanation.definitionFit: A pianist plays a keyboard instrument, so plays the keys.

clue.text: Quite shocked by partner's lead in card game

indicators.note: lead means the first letter, the one at the front of partner
shocked letters are jolted out of place, so the word quite is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is rather startled when their partner leads at the card table.
explanation.definitionFit: Piquet is an old two-player trick-taking game played with a 32-card pack.

clue.text: Losing head, cuddle with a north African

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the word for cuddle goes

parts.note: a hug is a cuddle
and means with, joining two things

explanation.surface: Someone in a panic embraces a person from the north of Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A Ugandan is a person from Uganda, a country in east Africa.

clue.text: Gives response concerning statutes

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading
acts of Parliament are statutes

explanation.surface: Someone replies on the subject of the law.
explanation.definitionFit: To react is to respond to something, so reacts means gives a response.

clue.text: Achieves satisfactory standard in new Maths, Greek and — after vacation — English

indicators.note: new means the letters are made afresh in a new order
a vacation empties a place, so the word and loses its middle

explanation.surface: A school report: the pupil hits the mark in modern maths, Greek and, after the holidays, English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after vacation' means 'and' is emptied of its middle letter; 'new' rearranges that with the two subjects, and English is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To make the grade is an idiom for reaching the required level.

clue.text: See 24
Coffee tax reduced after agreement from Merkel

indicators.note: after places the reduced tax behind the German yes

parts.note: ja is German for yes, as the former German chancellor would say

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the tax loses its last letter

parts.note: VAT, value added tax, is a tax

explanation.surface: The German chancellor agrees to a lower duty on coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Java is slang for coffee, after the Indonesian island where it was grown.

clue.text: She served David a litre of beer, you say?

indicators.note: you say signals that the phrase is spoken and heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a litre is a big ale, so the phrase spoken is a big ale

explanation.surface: A barmaid serves a customer a large beer and asks if that is what he ordered.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1 Samuel, Abigail brought supplies to David and called herself his servant before marrying him; an abigail is also a lady's maid.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical Abigail waited on King David as his handmaid and later wife.

clue.text: A small point that's relevant

parts.note: pt is the short form of point

explanation.surface: A minor remark that bears on the matter at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt means suitable or pertinent, so relevant to the matter.

clue.text: Soup: food cardinal rejected

parts.note: chow is slang for food

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the word for cardinal is reversed

parts.note: cardinal is a deep scarlet colour, so red

explanation.surface: A churchman turns up his nose at a bowl of soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Chowder is a thick soup, typically made with clams or fish.

clue.text: During day, ten can board a ship, showing intelligence

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to board a ship is to get onto it, so the piece goes inside a ship

parts.note: SS, steamship, is a ship

indicators.note: during says the ten falls within the day

parts.note: Tues is the abbreviation for Tuesday
taken as written

explanation.surface: On a given day, ten people manage to get aboard a vessel, which shows good sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'During' puts the ten inside the day abbreviation to give TUTENES; 'board' then sets that inside the ship with A at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Astuteness is shrewdness, a sharp practical intelligence.

clue.text: Mean biddy regularly withheld name

indicators.note: every other letter of mean biddy is held back, leaving the alternate ones

explanation.surface: A stingy old woman routinely refused to give her name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly withheld' drops letters 1, 3, 5 and so on of MEANBIDDY, keeping the second, fourth, sixth and eighth.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is a woman's given name, as in the author Enid Blyton.
